AUDIT QUESTION: Batch 39 = RULING 23 (a) (orchestrator 2026-11-12 '13:18'): V1 (two vision models answer a checklist about a video's contact sheet; any 'no' fails the row) asked 'every talking-head segment shows its speaker centred in the frame' of a 9:16 segment laid out as a STACK (two speakers in two panels, one above the other), and one model answered no ('framed off-centre'). Now: verify_pack.stack_note names every 9:16 segment whose vertical-layout shots are a stack ('9:16 STACK clip_02 (Natalie Brunell): stack2: two speakers in two panels, one above the other; each face is centred in its own panel') in the layout note the vision prompt already carries; the checklist item vertical_speaker_centred adds: for a segment the layout note names as a STACK, answer about EACH face: each face centred in ITS OWN panel and no panel edge cutting through a face; the single-speaker question applies only to single-speaker layouts. Tests (both Heimdall vision models, the Nov 12 re-run's 9:16 frames): the untouched stack frame passes; the stack with its top face pushed into the panel edge fails; a single-speaker frame shifted off-centre fails.
FIND: any way a cropped face or an off-centre single speaker now passes; a non-stack segment getting the stack wording; tests that do not test what they claim. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

So if the layout note names it as STACK (because one shot is stack), the single-speaker question is suppressed for the whole segment. This is a real issue.

This is a legitimate concern. The note should describe the layout structure (two panels, one above the other) without asserting the centring, and let the checklist do the verification.
